content.user_title: Create Logos with Shared Semantic Structure
content.value_statement: Logo concepts often stack unrelated symbols or hide weak ideas behind visual polish. This skill builds and evaluates marks where multiple meanings share one coherent structure.
actual_capabilities: Determines whether semantic fusion is appropriate for a supplied logo brief.
Generates at least six thumbnails across three concept families and three fusion methods.
Scores candidates on brand fit, integration, distinctiveness, legibility, reproduction, and safety.
Supports design, redesign, critique, comparison, and prompt-only workflows.
Reviews rendered marks for size, monochrome, reverse, grayscale, and silhouette performance.
Defines production handoff requirements for variants, clear space, sizes, and exports.
limitations: The skill does not provide legal trademark clearance.
Visual quality cannot be verified without an actual rendered artifact.
Unfamiliar scripts and cultural meanings require review by a fluent or qualified person.
The workflow does not replace a complete brand identity process.

use_cases.title: Develop an Integrated Brand Mark
use_cases.description: Turn two important brand signals into distinct concept families that share contours, strokes, voids, or modules.

use_cases.title: Review a Fusion Logo
use_cases.description: Assess whether a supplied mark is structurally integrated, legible, reproducible, distinctive, and culturally appropriate.

use_cases.title: Compare Design Candidates
use_cases.description: Apply consistent scoring and hard gates to several concepts, then identify a winner or reject every candidate.

prompt_templates.title: Check Brief Fit
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate whether semantic fusion fits this logo brief: [brief]. Identify the signals, shared structures, constraints, assumptions, and recommended design route.
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner evaluation of a new brief

prompt_templates.title: Create Concept Families
prompt_templates.prompt: Develop six thumbnails across three semantic-fusion families for [brand]. Vary the semantic pairing, silhouette, and method. Explain each shared structural move.

prompt_templates.title: Critique a Rendered Mark
prompt_templates.prompt: Critique the attached logo against this brief: [brief]. Report evidence, hard-gate failures, scores, required tests, and the smallest useful revisions.

prompt_templates.title: Compare and Prepare Handoff
prompt_templates.prompt: Compare these logo candidates using identical criteria and hard gates. Select a winner or reject all, then define pending QA and production handoff requirements.

output_examples.input: Create a mark combining the letter A with a mountain ascent for an outdoor coaching brand.
output: Applicability: suitable, because the diagonal letter structure can also describe an ascent.
Family direction: one shared peak and crossbar form, tested against arrow and mountain clichés.
Status: concept only; visual QA and similarity screening remain pending.

output_examples.input: Critique a logo that places a complete leaf icon inside a complete speech bubble.
output: Finding: the symbols coexist but do not share a contour, stroke, void, or module.
Revision: rebuild the leaf vein as part of the speech bubble tail and retest the silhouette.

output_examples.input: Compare three app icon concepts for legibility and semantic integration.
output: Candidate B leads because its shared negative space survives the committed icon size.
Candidate A fails reverse use, while Candidate C relies on color for the second reading.
Production status remains pending until mask, crop, and vector-path checks are complete.

best_practices: State the smallest committed size, required scripts, and must-keep elements before concept generation.
Test black and white geometry before adding color, effects, or mockups.
Record prior-art sources and unresolved similarities without claiming legal clearance.
anti_patterns: Do not stack complete icons and describe the result as semantic fusion.
Do not claim visual quality, originality, or production readiness without running the relevant checks.
Do not preserve clever fusion when it harms recognition, script legibility, or cultural safety.

faq.question: What is semantic fusion in logo design?
faq.answer: It makes two or more brand meanings depend on the same contour, stroke, void, glyph structure, or module system.

faq.question: Can this skill create a complete brand identity?
faq.answer: No. It focuses on integrated logo concepts, evaluation, and proportionate handoff requirements.

faq.question: Does this skill perform trademark clearance?
faq.answer: No. It supports design-direction similarity screening, which is not jurisdiction-specific legal clearance.

faq.question: Can it review an existing logo?
faq.answer: Yes. Critique mode reports evidence, hard-gate failures, a decision, and minimal revisions.

faq.question: Does it need a rendered image?
faq.answer: A rendered artifact is required for visual quality claims. Prompt-only work must keep visual checks unverified.

faq.question: How are unfamiliar scripts handled?
faq.answer: The workflow requires authoritative references and review by a fluent reader before production release.
